Gold.note: Central bank buying and rate cut expectations support continued upside despite elevated levels.

Silver.note: Dual industrial and monetary demand coupled with persistent structural deficits drive bullishness.

Copper.note: Green energy transition demand and tight smelter treatment charges support a structural deficit.

Uranium.note: Structural supply deficits and renewed global nuclear capacity build-outs underpin strong pricing.

Lithium.note: Near-term supply surplus from new African and Australian projects continues to weigh on prices.

Nickel.note: Persistent oversupply from Indonesian HPAL projects and sluggish EV demand growth cap upside.

Zinc.note: Recent mine closures and low treatment charges indicate a tightening global concentrate market.

Iron Ore.note: Ongoing weakness in Chinese property construction and high seaborne supply limit price recovery.

Coal.note: Peaking global thermal demand and ample seaborne supply offset resilient metallurgical coal markets.

Rare Earths.note: Chinese export controls provide a floor, but sluggish EV motor demand limits near-term upside.

Manganese.note: Weak global steel production offsets supply disruptions from South African logistical bottlenecks.

PGM.note: Weak internal combustion engine auto sales and high above-ground inventories weigh on near-term pricing.

Potash.note: Normalizing supply chains from Russia and Belarus keep global inventories adequately stocked.

Aluminum.note: Capacity caps in China and rising green energy demand support a tightening global balance.

Diversified.note: Broad exposure to copper and iron ore provides a balanced risk profile amid mixed macro signals.
